raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The clinical history of dry heaving and stifled sneeze (Valsalva maneuver) causing sudden neck/chest pain, combined with radiographic findings of linear lucencies along the paratracheal/hilar regions extending into the neck (subcutaneous emphysema), is classic for spontaneous pneumomediastinum caused by alveolar rupture (Macklin effect). There is no evidence of pleural effusion, lung abscess, or large pneumothorax to support the other options.
